summary: A battered round stone tower with a corbelled crenellated crown, a conical cap and banner, arrow slits spiralling up the shaft, and an outside stair to a raised door.
objective: Seen from about seventeen metres the tower reads as three tiers: tapered shaft with a crenellated crown and cone cap, then merlons, corbel ring and string courses, then merlon capstones, worn tread nosings and banner ties.
example_prompts: Put a watchtower on the ridge above the village.
I need a round tower with a stair up to a raised door.
not_for: Any claim about the defensive design or masonry of a specific historical tower.

silhouette: shaft tapering from a 5.24 m splayed plinth to a 3.5 m crown, so the outline is never a parallel-sided tube
crenellated crown and conical cap breaking the sky, with a banner pole reaching 11.97 m
external stair wedge running 4.8 m out from the tower centre to the raised door at 1.7 m
medium: fourteen merlons with embrasures between them around a corbel ring that projects 34 cm past the shaft
five projecting string courses dividing the shaft, plus the splayed plinth at the base
five arrow slits climbing the shaft on a slow spiral, each in a dressed frame standing 14 cm proud of the curved wall so the recess reads without cutting a hole in the drum
an emissive first-floor window with glazing bars, and a seven-voussoir semicircular arch over the recessed plank door
a landing on two corbels at door height, reached by a seven-step flight
fine: a lighter capstone on every third merlon, 14 cm thick, chamfered on its arris
worn lighter nosing on each stair tread, seeded in length so no two rub the same
a lighter keystone at the crown of the door arch, and every voussoir yawed back onto the curve of the drum rather than laid on one flat plane
three banner panels each hanging at a different seeded angle

principles: A round tower lives or dies on its batter. A cylinder with parallel sides reads as a silo at every distance.
The crown is where the reading happens: corbel ring, then merlons, then cap. Three stacked rings give a tower more identity than any amount of surface detail.
A defensive door is raised and reached by a stair to a landing; putting it on the ground plane throws away the whole idea.
An arch on a round tower must follow the drum. Seven voussoirs laid on one flat plane read as scattered blocks; the same seven yawed onto the curve read as an arch.
implementation: Call create({ height, baseRadius, topRadius, merlons, slits, doorHeight, seed }); the shaft is centred on the origin with y = 0 at the ground.
Attach a flag, brazier or lantern through the banner, walkway and lantern sockets.
The first-floor window carries an emissive material, so a night look reads without post-processing.
observable_checks: Run scripts/kit-proof.py and count features in close.png: at least two from each detail-ladder band must be visible in the frame.
topRadius below baseRadius always: equal radii remove the batter and the tower stops reading as masonry.
Two instances with different seeds move the arrow slits around the shaft and re-rub the tread nosings.

known_limits: Authored creative geometry. Nothing here is a measurement of any real tower, fortification or material.
The poly budget is the triangle count observed at default parameters; 22 merlons and 8 slits cost about 6600 triangles.
footprint_m is the plinth diameter. The stair carries the built bounding box out to 7.8 m in +Z, which a layout must allow for.
The shaft is a single tapered drum at 24 radial segments; at very close range the silhouette is faceted rather than round.
Tuned against ACESFilmic tone mapping at exposure 1.0 with no post-processing.
The shaft is a solid drum: openings are dressed surrounds standing proud of the curved wall rather than holes cut through it, which reads correctly from outside and not at all from within.
creative_affordances: Any parameter may be pushed outside its stated range; the range is the band that was proved, not a limit.
Drop the cap and raise merlons for a ruin, or lift doorHeight to 3 m and lengthen the stair for a keep.

defaults.rationale: A 0.45 m batter over 8 m is about 3 degrees, enough to read at the mid proof distance without looking like a cone, and 14 merlons around a 3.8 m crown give a 0.85 m pitch that stays countable in the close frame.
